grammatical_complexity.notes: Dominated by present simple and present perfect in a conversational style. Present perfect appears frequently throughout. One third conditional and one first conditional. Relative clauses recur. The mix of simple and complex structures with present perfect as a noticeable minority places this at level 3.

cultural_reference_load.notes: Most references (Duolingo, Reddit, AirBNB, Google Maps, Real Madrid) are globally known brands/topics a Latin American adult would recognize. The 40-hour work week and overtime concept is mildly culturally specific but understandable from context. No North American-specific customs that would block comprehension.

sentence_structure.notes: Dialogue format with many short conversational turns. Mostly subject-verb-object with some compound sentences using 'but' and 'and'. A few longer sentences with subordinate clauses but average remains moderate. Occasional run-on instructions ('Read to increase vocabulary. Learn the real pronunciation.') but these are short imperatives.

items.context: people who've actually learned a language before
items.reason: Spanish speaker may interpret 'actually' as 'actualmente' (currently), creating confusion about whether the advice comes from people who are currently learning vs. people who have genuinely learned.

items.context: you'll only know if it works once you have to use it in the workplace
items.reason: While 'once' looks like the Spanish word for 'eleven,' the context makes it clear this means 'when/as soon as.' The sentence structure ('once you have to use it') would not make sense with the number eleven, so the trap is neutralized.
